items.label: f01-pto-type-migration-plan
items.front: Drill: adding PtoType to the HRIS. What must your migration plan cover?
items.back: API contract, entity, DbContext configuration, seed data, UI, tests and rollback - and, since there are no migrations yet, introducing migrations (MigrateAsync instead of EnsureCreatedAsync) first.

items.label: f03-junior-vs-senior-ids
items.front: Two junior claims: 'the DTO has a Guid' and 'the form has required fields'. What does a senior ask for each?
items.back: Is the id scoped to the actor's permissions? What does the server reject?

items.label: f02-contract-drift
items.front: What risk does the critique see between Contracts.cs and the React client's types.ts, and the fix?
items.back: UI/API contract drift (medium): hand-written C# DTOs and TS types can diverge silently. Add contract tests or a generated OpenAPI client.

items.prompt: GET /api/employees/{id} lets any authenticated user fetch any employee profile, while GET /api/pto filters by employee/manager visibility. How does the IDOR checklist treat the profile endpoint?

choices.text: As equivalent to the PTO list, which is unfiltered too
As safe, because employee ids are random GUIDs
As a confirmed IDOR that must return 404 instead
As possibly intended for a directory, to confirm

choices: As equivalent to the PTO list, which is unfiltered too
As safe, because employee ids are random GUIDs
As a confirmed IDOR that must return 404 instead
As possibly intended for a directory, to confirm

items.explanation: IDOR is about accessing resources you do not own; whether a staff directory should be visible is a product decision to confirm.

items.prompt: If you owned this HRIS for three months, what does the critique put first?

choices.text: Integration tests for login, PTO visibility, approvals and audit
Adding pagination and limits to the org chart and employee list
Replacing ToLower().Contains search with full-text search
Splitting Program.cs into endpoint groups and small services

choices: Integration tests for login, PTO visibility, approvals and audit
Adding pagination and limits to the org chart and employee list
Replacing ToLower().Contains search with full-text search
Splitting Program.cs into endpoint groups and small services

items.explanation: There are no automated tests at all while critical auth logic lives in Program.cs; tests come before refactors.

items.prompt: The guide finds no hosted service, queue, outbox, email sender or retry policy. How does it characterise that?

choices.text: As a critical defect that loses approvals
As background work hidden in middleware
As proof the API cannot run in production
As a design boundary, not a bug

choices: As a critical defect that loses approvals
As background work hidden in middleware
As proof the API cannot run in production
As a design boundary, not a bug

items.explanation: Its drill designs a PtoNotificationOutbox written in the same transaction and processed by a BackgroundService.

items.prompt: The critique rates the JWT signing key in appsettings.json as a high risk. What is the recommendation?

choices.text: Rotate the key automatically on every application start
Move the secret into user-secrets or environment config
Switch from JWT bearer tokens to cookie authentication
Shorten the key so it is harder to brute-force offline

choices: Rotate the key automatically on every application start
Move the secret into user-secrets or environment config
Switch from JWT bearer tokens to cookie authentication
Shorten the key so it is harder to brute-force offline

items.explanation: A committed development key would let anyone mint valid tokens if reused outside development.

items.prompt: When HR approves a PTO request, how are the balance deduction and the audit entry persisted?

choices.text: Only the audit entry; the balance is recomputed on read
The audit entry first, then the balance in a separate transaction
Together, in one SaveChangesAsync call
The balance first, then the audit entry in a background job

choices: Only the audit entry; the balance is recomputed on read
The audit entry first, then the balance in a separate transaction
Together, in one SaveChangesAsync call
The balance first, then the audit entry in a background job

items.explanation: Saving both in one SaveChanges gives one implicit transaction, so the audit cannot exist without the balance change or vice versa.

items.prompt: What stops a repeated approval call from double-deducting an employee's PTO balance?

choices.text: The client disabling the approve button after one click
An idempotency key stored alongside each PTO decision
A unique index on the audit log for each request id
Closed requests (approved, rejected, cancelled) return 409

choices: The client disabling the approve button after one click
An idempotency key stored alongside each PTO decision
A unique index on the audit log for each request id
Closed requests (approved, rejected, cancelled) return 409

items.explanation: The guide lists it under idempotency; balance update and audit then save together in one SaveChangesAsync.

items.prompt: The critique suspects ToLower().Contains employee search may become slow. How does it treat that claim?

choices.text: As a security issue because it allows SQL injection
As irrelevant because SQLite indexes text columns automatically
As a confirmed defect to fix immediately
As a hypothesis to measure with data before optimising

choices: As a security issue because it allows SQL injection
As irrelevant because SQLite indexes text columns automatically
As a confirmed defect to fix immediately
As a hypothesis to measure with data before optimising

items.explanation: The guide separates confirmed findings (no tests, CI, migrations, workers) from hypotheses that need evidence.

items.prompt: A Manager calls POST /api/pto/{id}/decision. Which two resource-level checks can make the server answer Forbid?

choices.text: The PTO dates overlap a public holiday, or the request starts in the past
The manager lacks the PeopleOps policy, or the hours exceed the balance
The employee is not their direct report, or the request is at the HR stage
The manager's JWT is over an hour old, or the employee is in another department

choices: The PTO dates overlap a public holiday, or the request starts in the past
The manager lacks the PeopleOps policy, or the hours exceed the balance
The employee is not their direct report, or the request is at the HR stage
The manager's JWT is over an hour old, or the employee is in another department

items.explanation: Resource-level authorization lives inside the PTO decision handler: direct-manager ownership, and managers are blocked from HR-stage final approval.

items.prompt: SeedData calls EnsureCreatedAsync and returns early if any employee exists. What is the consequence for schema changes?

choices.text: The early return reseeds any tables whose shape has changed
With no migration history, model changes never reach an existing database
Schema changes are harmless, because SQLite ignores unknown columns
EnsureCreatedAsync applies pending model changes at every startup

choices: The early return reseeds any tables whose shape has changed
With no migration history, model changes never reach an existing database
Schema changes are harmless, because SQLite ignores unknown columns
EnsureCreatedAsync applies pending model changes at every startup

items.explanation: EnsureCreated only creates a missing database. The guide's plan: add migrations, swap to Database.MigrateAsync, test up/down on a copy, keep seeds idempotent.

items.prompt: A junior says the Approvals tab is hidden for employees, so approvals are protected. What does a senior ask?

choices.text: Does the hidden tab reappear after a full page refresh?
What happens if the user posts directly to the endpoint?
Is the tab hidden with CSS, or removed from the DOM entirely?
Is the tab also hidden on the mobile layout breakpoints?

choices: Does the hidden tab reappear after a full page refresh?
What happens if the user posts directly to the endpoint?
Is the tab hidden with CSS, or removed from the DOM entirely?
Is the tab also hidden on the mobile layout breakpoints?

items.explanation: UI hiding is not authorization; only the server's checks decide.

items.prompt: Department.LeadEmployee uses set-null on delete. What happens when the lead employee is removed?

choices.text: The delete is refused until a new lead is assigned
The department survives with no lead
The lead role passes to the longest-serving employee
The department is deleted along with its lead

choices: The delete is refused until a new lead is assigned
The department survives with no lead
The lead role passes to the longest-serving employee
The department is deleted along with its lead

items.explanation: Set null lets the lead go without deleting the department; contrast with Restrict on employee-to-department, which protects employee records.

items.prompt: The Employee-to-Manager relationship is configured with DeleteBehavior.Restrict. What does that prevent?

choices.text: An employee's manager being changed after the hire date
An employee being set as their own manager by mistake
Direct reports being loaded without an explicit Include call
A manager's deletion cascading through their direct reports

choices: An employee's manager being changed after the hire date
An employee being set as their own manager by mistake
Direct reports being loaded without an explicit Include call
A manager's deletion cascading through their direct reports

items.explanation: Restrict refuses the delete while dependents exist, so the org chart is not wiped out by one removal.
